Anna (Platform): Quick thought exercise — where should we stamp hosting-mode + tenant-ish metadata on telemetry (traces/metrics/logs) so hosted/dedicated/private all look consistent?
Tariq: Do you mean a header we attach at ingress, or a control-plane mutation after routing?
Anna (Platform): Exactly that question. If we stamp in the front proxy (ingress), we get consistency but risk leaking stuff before any private-mode redaction.
Maria: For private deployments the control plane is optional or customer-managed. If control plane adds metadata we lose parity with hosted.
Jonah: My take: runtime adapter (the component that actually speaks to models) seems like the common choke point across modes. Stamp there and propagate.
Tariq: +1 on runtime adapter, but what about request provenance? e.g., if a request is proxied through a partner, adapter might not have original tenant id. We should define a canonical header.
Anna (Platform): Proposal: require an RPC header from the ingress called `x-rw-inbound-mode` that contains {mode, origin, minimal-tenant}. Runtime adapter trusts it but validates signature if present. For private mode, header must be signed by control plane or omitted.
Maria: Signed header seems heavy for self-hosted. Some customers won't have a control plane to sign. Could we accept unsigned but flag as "untrusted"?
Jonah: Yes — add a trust bit. Downstream telemetry should include stamping source: stamped_by = [ingress|controlplane|adapter] and trust_level = [trusted|untrusted]. That keeps consumers aware.
Tariq: Also we must avoid putting any raw PII into headers. Use hashed tenant IDs (salted) or ephemeral fingerprints.
Anna (Platform): Agreed. We'll standardize on `tenant_hash` (sha256 truncated) + `tenant_scope` (billing|ops|unknown). No raw emails.
Maria: Sampling-wise, billing needs accurate per-tenant counts. If we stamp at adapter but sample early, billing counters break. We need deterministically sampled counters or a counter stream that is un-sampled.
Jonah: Implementation detail: two telemetry streams — counters (no sampling) for billing/cost and traces/logs (sampled). Adapter increments counters locally and forwards batches to telemetry ingesters.
Anna (Platform): Ops question: who owns schema? Is this runtime team's responsibility or telemetry/platform?
Tariq: Schema owned by platform, runtime implements stable minimal contract: header names, tenant_hash format, stamped_by enumeration. We'll version it.
Maria: Rollout plan idea: 1) adapter-side stamp in dev + staging (untrusted), 2) add header validation in hosted ingress, 3) provide doc + migration for dedicated/private.
Anna (Platform): Sounds good. Action items: Tariq to draft header + schema v1; Jonah to prototype adapter-stamping patch; Maria to write rollout checklist for Private customers (redaction guidance). I'll own coordination and docs. :thumbsup:
infra-bot: Deploy bot: created epic INF-telemetry-stamp-2026 (link: https://go/rw/INF-telemetry-stamp-2026)
Tariq: I'll start the spec this afternoon. If folks want to add constraints (retention, PII rules), drop them here or in that epic.
Maria: One more: we should log the stamping decision in traces (stamping_reason) so audit can retroactively explain mismatches.
Jonah: Good call. Include `stamping_reason` with values like `ingress-signature`, `adapter-default`, `controlplane-annotated`.
Anna (Platform): OK closing — thanks all. We'll reconvene after the draft is up.
